cardDescription: A white cloth becomes a smiling pretend spirit at the porch.
focus: The setting is a Friendly Ghost Made from a Sheet. Match each clue to a thing, action, or description in that scene.
solvingTip: Begin with a short answer you recognize. Use its crossing letters to work toward the longer scene words.
words: Rest on top of water rather than sink
Covered area at a house entrance
Clothing worn to play a character
A little frightening in a playful way
Happy expression with an upturned mouth

answerNotes.SHEET: Sheet can name paper, bed linen, or a flat baking pan. The scene tells whether the material is paper, cloth, or metal.
answerNotes.WHITE: White is a color description, not a flower or bird name. Crossings can help when a clue asks for a color rather than a species.
answerNotes.HANG: Hang means support something from above. A hook, cord, or branch can hold the weight while the object hangs below.
answerNotes.PORCH: A porch is an outdoor entrance area, often with a roof. A patio is usually a paved sitting area at ground level.
answerNotes.HALLOWEEN: The ghost, witch, and bat scenes are pretend seasonal decorations. They do not ask the reader to accept supernatural claims.
answerNotes.CLOTH: Cloth means fabric. A cloth used for wiping is an object made from that material, not a different substance.

answerNotes.HAT: A hat covers the head. The brim projects outward, while the crown is the part above it.
answerNotes.POINT: Point names a tapered end. A sharpened pencil needs a usable point, while a worn one makes a broader mark.
answerNotes.HANDLE: A handle is the part made for the hand to grip. Its shape depends on whether the object is carried, pulled, poured, or turned.
answerNotes.HALLOWEEN: The ghost, witch, and bat scenes are pretend seasonal decorations. They do not ask the reader to accept supernatural claims.
answerNotes.BUCKLE: A buckle fastens a belt or strap. Its pin can fit into different holes to adjust the length.
answerNotes.RIBBON: A ribbon is a narrow fabric strip. A looped bow and a straight trailing tail are different parts of a tied ribbon decoration.

answerNotes.PAPER: Paper can be folded, cut, and written on. Card stock is heavier and stiffer, making it useful for tags and greeting cards.
answerNotes.WING: Wings help birds, many insects, and airplanes fly, but their structures differ. The model-airplane scene uses a fixed surface rather than feathers.
answerNotes.FOLD: Folding brings one part of a sheet over another. A crease is the line left by pressing that fold.
answerNotes.CUT: Cut is an action, unlike a tool name such as scissors or knife. Matching the clue's part of speech helps narrow the answer.
answerNotes.SCISSORS: Scissors use two blades moving past one another. Finger loops help control the opening and closing action.
answerNotes.STRING: String is a thin cord used for tying or flying a kite. A kite's string connects the flying frame to the person holding it.
answerNotes.HANG: Hang means support something from above. A hook, cord, or branch can hold the weight while the object hangs below.
answerNotes.WINDOW: A window admits light through glass. A screen is a mesh barrier that can keep insects out when the glass is open.
answerNotes.HALLOWEEN: The ghost, witch, and bat scenes are pretend seasonal decorations. They do not ask the reader to accept supernatural claims.
answerNotes.POINT: Point names a tapered end. A sharpened pencil needs a usable point, while a worn one makes a broader mark.
answerNotes.NIGHT: Night is the dark part of the daily cycle. Dusk is the fading-light period around the approach of night.

answerNotes.SWEET: Sweet describes flavor, not temperature or texture. A food can be sweet and cold, or sweet and warm.
answerNotes.PAPER: Paper can be folded, cut, and written on. Card stock is heavier and stiffer, making it useful for tags and greeting cards.
answerNotes.HALLOWEEN: The ghost, witch, and bat scenes are pretend seasonal decorations. They do not ask the reader to accept supernatural claims.
answerNotes.PORCH: A porch is an outdoor entrance area, often with a roof. A patio is usually a paved sitting area at ground level.
answerNotes.DOOR: A door is the movable panel at an entrance. Hinges let it swing, while a latch or lock holds it closed.
answerNotes.BELL: A bell rings when a clapper or striker vibrates it. A school bell and a decorative handbell use that same basic sound-making idea.
answerNotes.SHARE: Share means give part of something to others. In a meal setting it can concern food rather than dividing property or money.
